transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM); Angela Martinez (CISO, Crestline), Tom Rivera (Head of Infra), Liam O'Neal (Compliance)

Summary: quick posture review to validate Redwood's SOC2/ISO evidence and operational controls before pilot sign-off. Discussed trust center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO integrations, audit logging, KMS options, and data residency.

00:00 Jordan Lee: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, this is Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, and then Priya our SE, Maya CSM. Angela, Tom, Liam, great to have you. We'll run about an hour.
00:18 Angela Martinez: Thanks Jordan. We'll kick off — main ask is: we need to validate SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture and see how Redwood maps to our control framework. Also KMS, audit logs and whether we can get trust center access.
00:34 Priya Kapoor: Yep, that's exactly what we want to cover. We'll walk through the reports we publish, how to access the trust center, and then dig into controls mapping. If it helps we can share a spreadsheet mapping our controls to typical SOC/ISO controls.
00:48 Tom Rivera: On the infra side, biggest things are RBAC and SAML integration — we use Okta and expect SCIM provisioning. Also key management — we require BYOK for production keys.
01:07 Priya Kapoor: Totally. Quick note on terminology, sometimes our transcripts say "SOC two" but it's SOC 2 Type II, and ISO 27001 — we refer to the certificate and scope. Our trust center is at trust.redwood.com (we'll send link).
01:27 Liam O'Neal: Can you confirm whether audit logs are tamper-evident and exportable to our SIEM? Retention policy?
01:39 Jordan Lee: Yes, great question. We provide near-real-time audit logs via the Console and export to customer S3 or you can push to your SIEM via our webhook. Retention defaults to 90 days for hosted, but Dedicated/Private can be configured longer per contract.
01:55 Angela Martinez: And are those logs signed or hashed? We need chain-of-custody for some controls.
02:05 Priya Kapoor: Logs include an integrity hash and append-only indexes — I'll caveat that the implementation detail depends on deployment mode; we'll note exact hashing details in the controls mapping doc.
02:20 Jordan Lee: For KMS, we support customer-managed keys — you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) using AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or an external HSM via our private deployment. For hosted, we offer optional CMEK via partner KMS.
02:40 Tom Rivera: When you say "CMEK" — customer-managed encryption keys — does Redwood ever hold unencrypted copies?
02:49 Priya Kapoor: No, not for the KMS-protected data. For metadata and logs there are different encryption scopes; we'll detail which artifacts are encrypted with which keys in the mapping.
03:05 Angela Martinez: About ISO 27001 — can you confirm scope? Is it just the hosted control plane or does it include Dedicated?
03:15 Jordan Lee: Our ISO scope covers the Redwood hosted control plane and the managed inference service; Dedicated and Private deployments are covered under contractual addendum — we have separate attestations for those deployments. We'll share exact certificate PDF and scope page.
03:31 Liam O'Neal: Do you have a controls mapping that ties Redwood controls to common frameworks? It helps us to fill our GRC tool.
03:40 Priya Kapoor: Yes, we maintain a controls matrix mapping to SOC 2 and ISO controls plus typical NIST and CIS references. We'll attach a Redwood->SOC2/ISO workbook.
03:52 Angela Martinez: Any recent penetration test results or third-party vuln scans?
04:00 Jordan Lee: We do annual pentests and quarterly vulnerability scans. The pentest exec summary is available through the Trust Center, full reports under NDA. We'll provide redacted executive summaries and details as needed.
04:18 Tom Rivera: For RBAC, how granular is the role model? We need separate roles for billing, infra ops, app owners.
04:28 Priya Kapoor: Our RBAC supports role-based policies and per-organization roles. For SSO we support SAML for authentication and SCIM for provisioning roles and groups. We can map Okta groups to Redwood roles.
04:43 Angela Martinez: And SCIM provisioning sync frequency?
04:48 Priya Kapoor: Default is near real-time provisioning via SCIM, but we can set sync windows if you have constraints.
05:00 Jordan Lee: Quick note on data residency — hosted can be pinned to region (US, EU currently). For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
05:12 Tom Rivera: For our European patients we need all PHI to remain in EU. Is there any multi-tenant risk?
05:21 Priya Kapoor: For hosted multi-tenant there is logical separation; Dedicated gives you physical isolation. For PHI workloads we typically recommend Dedicated with customer-managed keys and contract language.
05:35 Liam O'Neal: About logging export formats — will it be JSON?
05:39 Priya Kapoor: Yes JSON lines, schema v2, and we can provide schema doc in the mapping.
05:46 Angela Martinez: Who will be our main contact for the Trust Center access?
05:50 Jordan Lee: Maya will own Trust Center provisioning; she'll follow up after the call.
06:00 Maya Chen: I'll need a list of names and emails to add; also we'll attach the SOC2 Type II PDF and ISO certificate link.
06:12 Angela Martinez: Great.

[--- mid-call technical deep dive, some cross talk, minor transcription artifacts ---]

15:02 Priya Kapoor: On the controls mapping, example mapping: SOC 2 CC6.1 maps to our incident response process, ISO A.16 maps similarly — we'll put exact control IDs in the spreadsheet. Apologies if I mispronounce some IDs.
15:18 Tom Rivera: For the KMS flow, can we rotate keys on our schedule?
15:24 Priya Kapoor: Yes, for BYOK you control rotation. For CMEK there is an API to rotate and we can automate it with your KMS.
15:33 Liam O'Neal: Are audit logs available for every administrative action, like role changes and key rotations?
15:41 Priya Kapoor: Yes, we log admin events including role changes, key usage, key rotation events, and they include actor ID, timestamp, and request context.
15:50 Angela Martinez: Is there any PII in logs by default? We're sensitive about that.
15:57 Jordan Lee: Logs are redacted for user content; metadata includes request IDs and non-PHI context. We can set additional redaction rules for Dedicated.
16:10 Tom Rivera: For Dedicated, what's the provisioning lead time?
16:14 Jordan Lee: Typically 6–8 weeks depending on capacity and region; expedited options exist for enterprise contracts.
16:23 Angela Martinez: Do you support sub-tenanting and separation for multiple internal business units?
16:29 Priya Kapoor: Yes, multi-org setup is supported; we can create separate orgs with separate RBAC and billing.

[--- later in call, clarifying compliance docs ---]

40:05 Jordan Lee: Action items recap will be at the end; but to call out — we'll share Trust Center links, SOC2 Type II, ISO certificate, controls mapping workbook, and schedule the KMS deep-dive.
40:20 Liam O'Neal: One more question on third-party subprocessors and data flow diagrams. We need a data flow map for PHI.
40:30 Priya Kapoor: Yep, we have a standard data flow diagram and sub-processor list; we'll include that in the Trust Center package.
40:40 Angela Martinez: Any firewall/VPC requirements for Private deployment?
40:44 Tom Rivera: (interrupting) we also need network peerings and strict egress rules.
40:47 Priya Kapoor: For Private we support VPC peering, private link, and IP allow-lists. We'll share the networking guide.

58:10 Jordan Lee: Alright, quick recap and next steps. Priya will upload the controls mapping and technical notes. Maya will provision Trust Center access and share SOC2/ISO PDFs. Angela to share Crestline's baseline controls and contacts. Jordan will follow up with Dedicated pricing and timelines. We'll schedule the KMS/RBAC deep-dive for March 11.
58:35 Angela Martinez: That sounds good. Appreciate the clarity.
58:44 Tom Rivera: Thanks everyone.
58:50 Jordan Lee: Thanks all — we'll follow up via email with links.
58:55 Maya Chen: Action items and next steps in email, and I'll add access.
59:05 END OF CALL

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (e.g., "kay-v cache" for KV cache) and numbering; we've left stutters and overlaps to preserve meeting fidelity.

Links & artifacts referenced: Trust Center (trust.redwood.com) - SOC 2 Type II executive summary (link), ISO 27001 certificate (link), Controls mapping spreadsheet (to be shared), Networking guide (to be shared).

- Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II report exec summary and ISO 27001 certificate via Trust Center (Maya) by 2025-03-06.
- Priya to provide controls mapping workbook (Redwood -> SOC/ISO) by 2025-03-07.
- Schedule KMS/RBAC technical deep-dive for 2025-03-11 (owner: Priya).
- Jordan to send Dedicated/Private pricing and lead times by 2025-03-07.
